The target is the legacy measure: the aggregate of a business date available before the officers start, and the cost alert sent within 15 minutes of the end of the rollup (DL11). edits.old: The deployment exposes the metric read behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics` with its query and its answer, owner rwb-agent (P10), as fixed by RWB-P10-E1063-CON. The run read `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` and the case read `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` are served by the same release under the baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-CON and are registered on the route with the metric read. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.
edits.new: The deployment exposes the metric read behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics` with the query parameters `agent`, `segment`, `version`, `from` and `to`, a declared page size and cursor, and its answer, owner rwb-agent (P10), as fixed by RWB-P10-E1063-CON. The page size, the cursor form, the maximum page and the member types of the aggregate element and the held-date status are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0617) and are contract values. The answer is computed and served by rwb-agent from its own `agent_run` and `agent_evaluation` rows in schema `rwb_agent`, and its aggregate element carries runs, answered, fallback, fallback rate at four decimals, latency p50 and p95, tokens, cost and the latest evaluation score; its held-date status carries the business date, the run state and the previous published date (GAP-0616; GAP-0617). The run read `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` and the case read `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` are served by the same release under the baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-CON and are registered on the route with the metric read. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.
